_comment: Cross-domain skills. A skill is a capability that is NOT specific to one agent's domain - the same machinery serves Grow, Legal, Accounting, Maintenance, etc., with only the domain-specific adapter differing. Listing a skill here is what makes it discoverable: an agent (or a department head reviewing its members) can ask which skills apply to it without that knowledge being hardcoded anywhere. Adding an adopter is a config change, not a code change - same rule as departments.json.

data_collection_quest.summary: Gamified collection of labelled domain data toward a threshold that makes downstream training/automation actually viable.
data_collection_quest.solves: An agent can't do part of its job because no labelled domain data exists, and collecting it is tedious enough that it never happens.
data_collection_quest.adapter_contract: Agent supplies: (1) a counter returning {label: verified_count}, (2) the label set, (3) a threshold justified by what the downstream consumer needs.
invariants: Threshold is set by the downstream trainer's real requirement, never by what makes a nice progress bar.
Automated candidates (web search, scrape) never count as progress until a human verifies them.

adopters.note: Cannabis leaf-condition photos. No public dataset exists and PlantVillage models cover pepper/potato/tomato only, so grower-supplied images are the only route to a working model.
Labelled contract clauses by type/risk. Would let clause spotting stop depending on a general model's guess.
Human-categorised transactions. Categorisation is currently LLM-guessed per call with no accumulating ground truth.
Telemetry windows labelled with what actually failed afterwards. Turns the existing trend check into a learned predictor.

candidate_sourcing.summary: Propose candidate examples from an external source (web search) when the operator cannot supply enough data themselves.
candidate_sourcing.solves: A collection campaign stalls because the operator's own environment cannot produce some labels (a condition their plant has never had, a contract type they've never signed).
invariants: Search PROPOSES, a human DISPOSES. A sourced candidate is never training data until reviewed.
Provenance (source URL, query, retrieval date) is recorded per candidate - a training set of unknown-origin images is a licensing and label-noise problem, not an asset.
Never used to 'validate' a prediction. Searching for a condition returns descriptions of that condition whether or not the sample shows it, which confirms rather than validates.

adopters.note: Sources candidate leaf-condition photos via searxng for labels the grower's own plant hasn't exhibited.
